comparison: Python buffered binary read(size) provides a bounded returned byte string; stat permits rejection before opening a known oversized regular file. This directly supplies the observed requirement without serializing content to a second process. The executable growth fixture verifies a five-byte request for a four-byte allowance.

Go io.LimitReader can limit bytes read, but reaching its limit produces EOF. A caller still needs an extra-byte overflow check and aggregate counters to avoid treating truncation as a complete document.

Java InputStream.readNBytes(len) also limits returned bytes. It is a credible alternative outside the component language, but requires the same overflow/cumulative accounting. Neither Java nor Go was benchmarked here; no throughput or latency advantage is asserted for any candidate.
rationale: KEEP Python for this narrow admission layer because its standard I/O API enforces the decisive bound within the same process that decodes and parses the document, preserving the tested path/error boundary without an additional content transfer.
